HomeEssentials Inc. - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the HomeEssentials Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. Following the prepared remarks, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I will now turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead, Sarah.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us on HomeEssentials Inc.'s Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. On the line with me today are Mike Thompson, our Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, our Chief Financial Officer; and David Rivera, our Chief Merchandising Officer.

As always, I'd like to remind everyone that today's discussion includes forward-looking statements within the meaning of federal securities laws. These statements are based on our current expectations but are subject to various risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our most recent SEC filings, including our Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a detailed discussion of factors that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll now turn the call over to Mike Thompson, our CEO.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to share HomeEssentials Inc.'s Q2 results, where we continued to execute against our strategic priorities and delivered resilient performance amid a tough macroeconomic backdrop, including lingering inflation and shifting consumer behaviors.

In today's call, I'll highlight five key areas of our performance. First, our overall results reflect disciplined markdown management in a promotional retail environment, balancing traffic generation with margin protection. Second, e-commerce momentum accelerated through highly effective digital marketing that's fueling store traffic and omnichannel sales. Third, store-level execution strengthened via advanced inventory optimization tactics. Fourth, we're making solid progress on our core strategic initiatives like fleet optimization and supply chain resilience. And fifth, our outlook remains constructive, with clear comp sales guidance signaling continued momentum.

We're well-positioned to navigate these dynamics and create lasting shareholder value. Now, I'll hand it over to Lisa Chen, our CFO, for a deeper dive into the financials.

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Mike, and good morning, everyone. I'll walk through our Q2 financial results in detail, starting with the top line. Total revenue reached $5.8 billion, up 3.2% from the prior year, driven by a 1.8% comp store increase and contributions from new units partially offset by closures.

Gross margin came in at 35.4%, reflecting pressure from elevated markdowns as we cleared seasonal inventory, though underlying merchandise margins expanded thanks to private label growth and shrink improvements. Operating expenses totaled $2.0 billion, or 34.5% of revenue, benefiting from productivity gains in labor and occupancy. This flowed through to net income of $320 million, or $1.45 diluted earnings per share. Operating cash flow was robust at $520 million, supporting share repurchases and debt reduction. Inventory stands at $4.2 billion, down 12% year-over-year, with weeks of supply at a five-year low of 28 weeks.

Our balance sheet remains rock-solid, with ample liquidity to fund growth priorities.

To give you more context on these results, let me unpack our markdown activity and its impact on margins, a vital element in our brick-and-mortar operations where pricing discipline and inventory turns are everything. In Q2, markdowns as a percentage of net sales rose to 11.8%, up 250 basis points from 9.3% last year, translating to about $285 million in markdown dollars versus $210 million in Q2 2023. This uptick was intentional, aimed at boosting traffic and comps against a backdrop of inflation squeezing essentials spending and apparel softness following an unusually mild winter influenced by El Niño patterns across the U.S.

By category, apparel and softlines drove 45% of markdowns, equating to 5.3% of that segment's sales, with heavy clearance on fall transition items like outerwear and knits that underperformed in the Northeast and Midwest. This aligns with industry trends—Macy's and Kohl's saw rates of 13-15% recently. Home goods and hardlines, 55% of sales, held markdowns to 7.2% of sales, mainly on patio and grilling seasonal stock, while electronics managed 4.1% due to constrained allocations from vendors like Samsung and LG.

This contributed to a 120 basis point gross margin decline to 35.4%, versus 36.6% last year and just below our 35.5-36.0% guide. Stripping out markdowns, core merchandise margins grew 80 basis points from better private label mix—Essentials Home up 15% year-over-year at 42% margins—and 30 basis point shrink reduction to 1.6% via RFID in 1,200 stores. Absent markdowns, margins would hit 37.2%, closer to historical levels.

Regionally, Sunbelt areas—Florida, Texas, Southwest—posted 9.5% markdowns on 28% of comps at +4.2%, yielding 37.1% margins boosted by outdoor category strength. Northeast markets spiked to 14.2% markdowns with flat comps at +0.1% from wet weather and office return lags, pulling margins to 33.8%. In Canada, our 150 stores hit 12.5% amid CAD strength and Walmart competition, offset by tailored assortments.

Inventory health is improving: total stock down 12% year-over-year, apparel weeks under 10 from 14, easing future risks. We're countering with an AI dynamic pricing tool from SymphonyAI, now on 70% of SKUs in 2,500 stores, leveraging comp shop, weather, and traffic data for 50-100 basis points of FY25 lift. Vendor scorecards with P&G and Whirlpool provide 2-3% overstock rebates, adding 15 basis points this quarter.

For Q3, expect 10.5-11.0% markdowns, margins of 35.8-36.3%, trending to 36.5% in H2 with leaner stocks. Our BOPIS surge—up 22%—helps against Amazon promo risks.

While markdowns weighed on the quarter, they're tactical for traffic and health in a value-driven market. Initiatives set us up for 37-38% long-term margins.

Building on that operational rigor, digital marketing effectiveness has been pivotal to our omnichannel flywheel, where stores still drive 72% of sales. It generated a 28% lift in store-attributed revenue year-over-year, countering soft sentiment and rising ad costs.

Blended ROAS hit 5.8x, up from 4.2x, exceeding our 5x goal. Search via Google and Bing delivered 7.2x on local terms like "nearest home essentials store" or "same-day pickup appliances." Meta yielded 4.9x, with Reels 35% ahead via shoppable videos; TikTok at 6.1x nabbed Gen Z for apparel and decor, akin to Target's social wins.

CAC dropped 22% to $14.50 per new customer, under our $18 breakeven, via loyalty app data (18 million users, 65% targeting) and Criteo retargeting cutting waste 40%. Multi-touch attribution shows digital aiding 42% of store conversions, up from 28%.

In the U.S. (68% spend), geofencing around 1,200 stores lifted local traffic 15% per Wi-Fi heatmaps; Dallas and Atlanta topped 7x ROAS on big-ticket ads. Northeast urban hit 9% uplift amid Amazon rivalry, boosted by Snapchat AR events. Europe (15% spend) held 4.5x ROAS cookieless via Trade Desk UID 2.0; Asia-Pacific stores in Australia/Japan reached 6.8x with LINE/Kakao, 25% BOPIS.

Tech upgrades include server-side tagging for 92% accuracy, AWS SageMaker bidding, and 30% UGC shift from #HomeEssentialsHaul. CTV pilots on Roku/Fire TV upped home goods traffic 18%.

Digital store sales enjoy 450 bps higher margins via BOPIS (22% orders); Klaviyo emails lift conversions 12%. FY24 $150 million AI capex eyes 7x ROAS.

This outperforms peers like Macy's 4.1x, powering growth beyond flat industry traffic.

Complementing these efforts, our inventory optimization strategies are yielding major gains against e-commerce speed and discounters. Q2 turnover rose 22% to 5.1x from 4.2x, days on hand to 71 from 87—top-quartile vs. Macy's 4.8x, matching Target's 5.2x. GMROI up 15% to 2.85; shrinkage to 1.2% from 1.7%.

Core is Blue Yonder AI forecasting with POS, weather, CPI data across 1,200 stores/15 DCs. Apparel errors down 28%, stockouts to 6.5%, conversion +4.2 points using Google Trends/TikTok signals. Northeast nailed outerwear; Europe improved 14% despite regs.

Omnichannel sync: 85% stores as hubs, BOPIS under 2 hours 92% time, ship-from-store $1.2B (18% e-comm). RFID on 70% SKUs, IoT shelves in 150 stores cut produce OOS 40%. ABC-XYZ prioritizes JIT for A-items; VMI with P&G/Unilever handles 25% C-items, saving $45M.

Supplier terms: 96% OTD, Asia sourcing 40% from Vietnam/Bangladesh (45-day leads), forward freight hedges. Private labels at 22% inventory turn 6.8x, +25% margins amid trade-down.

ESG: Writedowns down 35% to $28M, 95% slow-movers donated/recycled. Q3 targets 5.4x turns, $75M RFID capex for 3x ROI.

Challenges like apparel volatility persist, but with retail sales +2.8%, we're set for 8-10% comps.

Tying it together, here's an update on our key strategic initiatives fueling resilience versus inflation at 3.1%, Red Sea issues, and e-comm at 15% U.S. retail. Q3 comps hit 5.2% vs. NRF 3.8%; margins +120 bps to 38.4%.

Store fleet: 25 new Sunbelt openings (+7.1% regional comps), 15 Northeast closures (-80 bps SG&A). 120 Next-Gen remodels with workshops/BOPIS lockers: +14.2% comps, 2.3 turns.

Omnichannel: Digital 28% revenue (+6 points), BOPIS 32% e-comm, curbside 85% via Instacart. Loyalty 42% sales, 28M members +18% repeats; RFID 60% SKUs, OOS -25%.

Supply chain: 40% North America sourcing (-15 days leads, +250 bps margins); Atlanta micro-DC cuts costs 22%. Green Brick: 75% stores LED/solar (-28% energy), EPA recognition.

Sunbelt leads (+8.4% Texas); Canada +6.1%. FY24 EBITDA +8-10%, $450-500M capex.

Finally, on outlook, Q4 comps guide +2.0% to +3.0%, accelerating from Q3's 1.8% on traffic +1.2%, conversion +0.8%, $85 ticket. Apparel +3.5-4.5%; home flat to +1.5%; electronics/footwear +1-2%. Sunbelt +4-5%; Midwest/Northeast flat-+1%; West +1.5-2.5%.

FY25 +2.5-3.5%, Q1 +2-3% assuming 2.1% GDP, 2.5% PCE. RFID 80% stores (-20% OOS), curbside 95%; value focus, memberships to 55%. Risks: unemployment >4.2%, tariffs; $450M cash supports 25 remodels.

With that, I'll turn it over to David for merchandising insights.

David Rivera, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thanks, Lisa. In Q2, we successfully launched our Essentials Home Refresh line, featuring sustainable, small-ticket impulse items like bedding and decor. It's exceeded expectations, driving 25% comp growth in home furnishings and strong early sell-through rates across 85% of stores. We're thrilled with the customer response and have more launches teed up for holiday and back-to-school.

Now, Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for queuing questions: Please press star then one if you're using a touch-tone phone. Our first question is from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning, team. Thanks for the details. Can you provide more color on the impact of ongoing inflation pressures on your sales mix and traffic?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, John. Inflation has indeed been a headwind, particularly on everyday essentials, prompting consumers to trade down—Nielsen shows 62% of middle-income households doing so on non-essentials. This fueled our markdown strategy to maintain traffic, especially in apparel where mild winter lagged demand. However, it also shifted mix toward higher-margin private labels like Essentials Home, up 15%, and Sunbelt strength offset Northeast softness. Overall, it contributed to our 1.8% comps, with digital driving incremental visits to counter it.

Operator:
Thank you. Our next question comes from Emily Davis with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Davis (JPMorgan):
Thanks. What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Hi, Emily. For Q3, we're guiding comps to +2.0% to +3.0%, building on Q2 momentum with traffic and conversion gains from holiday campaigns and BOPIS expansion. Categories like apparel lead at +3.5-4.5%, home steady, regional divergence with Sunbelt at +4-5%. FY25 full-year +2.5-3.5%, supported by RFID, loyalty, and value engineering against macro risks.

Operator:
Thank you. Our next question is from Robert Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Robert Lee (Barclays):
Appreciate it. Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements and how they're supporting inventory goals?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Sure, Robert. We've localized 40% sourcing to North America, cutting lead times 15 days and dodging Red Sea freight spikes via hedges at $3,500 per FEU. New Atlanta micro-DC services 350 stores, down last-mile 22%; Blue Yonder AI and VMI with P&G/Unilever boosted turns to 5.1x. Vendor OTD at 96%, RFID rollout—all positioning us for Q3 5.4x and holiday ramp with leaner, faster stock.

Operator:
Thank you. Our next question comes from Anna Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Anna Patel (Morgan Stanley):
Good morning. On digital marketing, how sustainable is the ROAS lift, and any shifts in spend allocation?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Morning, Anna. The 5.8x blended ROAS is sustainable, driven by first-party data from our 18 million loyalty users and ML retargeting—CAC down 22% to $14.50. We're reallocating 30% to UGC and CTV pilots showing 18% traffic uplift, with $150 million FY24 AI capex targeting 7x. Regional focus like geofencing keeps it scalable for store flywheel.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the question-and-answer session. I'll now turn the call back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Operator, and thanks to everyone for your thoughtful questions. We're pleased with Q2 progress and our sharpened focus on omnichannel execution, inventory discipline, and strategic investments. This positions HomeEssentials to deliver on our long-term goals. Appreciate your support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's HomeEssentials Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Thank you all for joining us. Have a great day.
